2.59 Education. Educational attainment in 1970 for the study area ranged from 5.7 school years completed in Zapata County to 10.2 school years completed in Val Verde County. The State median for school years completed is 10.4 years.
2.60 Agriculture. Agriculture production is expected to increase over the next few years as national and world demands for food and fiber continue to increase. The 1973 agricultural production for the study area was $301 million with sources of earnings mainly from fruits, vegetable, grains, and livestock. The study area is a part of the Water Resources Council BEA Economic Areas 142, 143, and 144 and data extrapolated from these areas indicate a continuing growth through the year 2020 for agriculture. The projected increase is at an average annual rate of about 1.21 percent.
2.61 Irrigation. Although the Rio Grande basin contains more than 19 percent of the area of Texas, the basin contributes less than 14 percent of the total surface water irrigation in Texas. The Middle Rio Grande Valley, an area between Falcon and Amistad Reservoirs, irrigated 55,000 acres in 1974, 63,000 acres ir 1969, and 50,000 acres in 1964. The Lower Rio Grande Valley, a four county area  Cameron, Willacy, Hidalgo, and Starr irrigated 794,000 acres in 1974, 808,000 acres in 1969, and 819,000 acres in 1964. In 1974, Falcon Reservoir supplied 92 percent of the total water used for irrigation. Ground water contributed less than 1 percent and combined supplies (i.e., a mixture of ground and surface water) contributed about 7 percent. Until recently the basin trend in irrigated acreage has been upward since the first historical developments. General economic conditions, technological advances in irrigation equipment, climatic conditions, and other factors have influenced the development of irrigated agriculture. However, present irrigated acreage has stabilized to 745,000 acres in the Lower Rio Grande Valley and 75,000 acres in the Middle Rio Grande Valley because of the adjudicated water rights (TWDB, 1975).
2.62 Industry. Manufacturing trends for BEA Economic Areas 142, 143, and 144 indicate continuing growth through 2020. Manufacturing value averaged about $150 million in earr.ings for 1969 and is projected to increase at an average annual rate of 3.94 percent through 2020. This compares to the average annual growth rate of 3.98 percent through 2020. This compares to the average annual growth rate of 3.98 percent for the United States. Mineral production accounted for over $100 million in earnings for the study area in 1973 from natural gas, petroleum, sand, gravel, stone, and clay. The BEA Economic Areas 142, 143, and 144 project an average annual increase of about 0.46 percent for the mining industry through the year 2020.
2.63 Land Use. Rangeland is the dominant land use in the study area with 84 percent of the total area. Cropland is second with over 11 percent. The land use data tabulated from the current Conservation Needs Inventory show that range and cropland account for over 95 percent of the eight county study area. The same categories account for over 11 percent of the state total (table 11-6).
